Description: 158 recordings of 10 min (transport ventilator and pulse oximeter), each replayed in real time once per execution mode on each platform; six recordings were replayed a second time as control repetitions (164 runs per platform and execution mode).
AMD: Lenovo T14 Gen 4, AMD Ryzen 7 PRO 7840U, 32 GB RAM. PI: Raspberry Pi 5, 16 GB RAM.
ATOMIC: firing decision and reaction function run under the reactor's evaluation lock. NON_ATOMIC: only the firing decision runs under the lock.
label A1–A13 as in the manuscript; reactor = reactor id in the configuration. Rows not belonging to a reactor are labelled Replay (send delay of the replay) or device (replayed device channels).

Every input update arriving at a reactor first passes the per-channel logical-time gate: it is accepted only if its tag (timestamp, microstep) is strictly greater than the last tag accepted on that channel, otherwise DISCARDED (no state change). Each accepted update triggers an evaluation of the firing rules. FIRED: at least one rule was satisfied and the reaction function ran. Output tags are (T, 0) for a new maximum input timestamp T, otherwise (T, previous microstep + 1).
Latency statistics (S1) and steady-state load indicators (S5, columns *_steady*) exclude the first 30 s of each run. All other values cover the whole run.

*_median: statistic computed per run, then the median over runs. *_ci_lo / *_ci_hi: 95 % percentile-bootstrap confidence interval of that median over runs (2,000 resamples). *_pooled: statistic over all samples of all runs taken together. *_max: maximum over runs.

p50, p99, p999 = 50th, 99th, 99.9th percentile (linear interpolation). With fewer than 1,000 samples per run (A1–A8, A10), the per-run p999 lies between the two largest values of the run and is close to the run maximum.

The replay stamps every event with its scheduled send instant. Metrics ending in _net are measured from the actual send instant logged by the replay instead, and thus exclude the replay's own wake-up delay.
Latencies in ms unless stated otherwise; percentages in %; ppm = per million.
